column1: # C#: classes, structs, records and enums (listed as classes), interfaces, methods, constructors (listed as methods, named after the class),
# properties and events (listed as fields; auto, full, init-only and expression-bodied alike). Not definitions: a field, an indexer (it has no name), a delegate,
# a return type (`ILogger Logger()` defines Logger and no method called ILogger), a call, `new X(...)`, an `if` or `return` in a body.
# conditional.cs is the conditional-compilation fixture: `#if` groups that cut a method apart
# (a body or `;` behind the parameter list, `=>` behind `#if`, an attribute in its own group) are
# read with the first branch of each group; a definition that exists only in a branch that is

# returns.cs: a method whose return type is a user type (plain, generic, nullable, wrapped, in an interface with and without conditional compilation) defines the method and never a method named after the type.
